sections.heading: Temple Complex, Jageshwar
sections.content: Surrounded by dense forests of fur and pine trees right in the middle of the Almora town are the temples of Nanda Devi and Narsingh. 34 kms from Almora is the ancient Shiva temple complex at Jageshwar. This houses one of the 12 jyotirlingas in the country. This temple

sections.heading: Baijnath Temple
sections.content: Kausani has the famous temple complex of Baijnath in the Garur valley of Katyur. A group of ancient temples dating back to the twelfth and thirteenth century line the banks of the river, presenting a beautiful sight. The temples are famous for its carving stone work. The main 10th century temple houses a beautiful idol of Goddess Parvati chiselled in black stone.According to the local tales Shiva and Parvati are believed to have married at the confluence of the Gomati and Garur Ganga. Innumerable tales of Lord Shiva and Parvati make these temples a fascinating

sections.heading: Kedarnath Temple
sections.content: The temple of Kedarnath is dedicated to Lord Shiva. The temple is built of large, heavy and evenly cut grey stone slabs, and is considered to be more than 1000 years old. It has a garbhagriha where the conical rock formation is situated, and a mandapam for seating devotees.

sections.heading: Uttarakhand- Handicrafts- Metal and tweeds
sections.content: In Almora, Tamta mohalla is the hub of unique traditional copperware art of Almora. Coppersmiths are in abundance in Almora and their works are complete pieces of art. In addition to coppersmiths, Almora is also home to weavers. Traditional tweeds and shawls are another product of the local craft in Almora which reflect the artistic brilliance of the local craftsmen.

sections.heading: painting
sections.content: The art of Miniature painting flourished in Garhwal under the influence of Mughal and Western Pahari schools, and that too without any feudal patronage. The arts and crafts of Uttarkhand, of which an amazingly rich variety exists today, demand and indeed deserve a closer look. A rich

sections.heading: Uttarakhand- Handicrafts- Painting -Aipana
sections.content: The rural art of Kumaon known as aipana, a local adaptation of alpana, (plaster with fingers) is practiced by the women folk. The other sacred and dainty paintings of this region are the pitha, the seat of Siva worshipped on auspicious days and decorated with geometrical patterns and chowki (seat) of Lakshmi and Saraswati using floral and traditional patterns.

sections.heading: Uttarakhand- Handicrafts- Wall Painting
sections.content: In the Kumaon region, the usual wall paintings are known as the bar-boond (dash and dot). The pattern is made first by making a number of dots to outline the design and then joining those dots by lines of different colours. Each pattern is known by the number of dots used. For example in the pattern called masti-bar-mat, a composition of ten dots and the colours yellow, red, violet and green are used. The designs are mostly floral and very lively.

sections.heading: Uttarakhand- Handicrafts- Painting
sections.content: Kumaon is also famous for pattas, special pictures made on festival days depicting the particular deity connected with the festival as also the deity's various aspects that are worshipped on the occasion.

sections.heading: Uttarkhand- Handicrafts- Wood Carving
sections.content: The wood carving of the region is breathtaking for its simple beautiful designs. Wooden front doors carved with floral designs, animals and fishes standout for its simple beauty. The carving on ones front door is supposed to be symbolic of his prosperity. In Garhwal and Kumaon the facade of the upper storeys of the dwelling units are wooden and are artistically carved. Abundant in wood and wood product, the artisans of the region have designed simple and beautiful designs on carvings on doors, windows and ceilings in the houses of the region. These beautifully ornamented doors and windows have motifs, generally of the Gods or Goddesses, add to the richness of the carvings. The craftspersons also do specific latticework to fill in the open space of the windows in order to give a screen like effect.

sections.heading: Uttarakhand- Handicrafts- Ornaments
sections.content: In every part of Garhwal and Kumaon, traditional goldsmiths make traditional ornaments using motifs and patterns which are thousands of years old. The ornaments come in variety of gold, silver, copper and brass.

sections.heading: Uttarakhand- Fairs & Festivals
sections.content: Numerous fairs and festivals are celebrated all over Uttarkhand every year. In the Kumaon hills, the festivals celebrated are Uttarayani Mela, Shravan Mela, Gananath Mela and Dwarahat Mela. The Uttarayani Mela is held at a number of places including Bageshwar, Rameshwar, Salt Mahadev, Chitrashila (Ranibagh), Pancheshwar, etc. on fourteenth of January of every year. Two large fairs are held at Jageshwar, one on the occasion of Shivratri (February) and the other in the month of Shravan (July-August). A dip on the occasion in the Jat Ganga and Brahmakund, near the temple complex, is of great religious significance. Gananath is 47 km from Almora. A fair is held here every year on Kartik Poornima (October  November), when thousands of pilgrims come to worship Lord Shiva and Ganesh. Nanda Devi Mela are held at Almora, Nainital, Nauti, Dandidhara, Munsyari and Ranikhet, of which the Almora and Roopkund fairs are the most famous. At Almora, thousands of people take part in a procession carrying the dola of Nanda Devi. The Nanda Devi temple of Almora is the venue for the three day long Nanda Devi Fair. Of great religious and cultural significance, it is held at Nanda Devi Temple in memory of Goddesses Nanda and Sunanda. It is said to have started in Kumaon during the reign of Raja Kalyan Chand in the sixteenth Century. Nestled in the lap of nature Almora is one of the most beautiful places in Kumaon region. Just besides the city flows the Koshi (Kaushaki) and Suyal (Salmali) rivers. In the ninth century Almora was ruled by Katyur dynasty. By 16th century this place was ruled by Chandravanshi rulers. This town was established by King Balo Kalyan Chand in 1563. This place was the capital city of the Kumaon region. The forts, monuments and palaces evidence of the splendour this place had in the past.
